_why: The tag of every variant of the two wire unions, which are hand-maintained in
server/src/protocol.rs and client/src/protocol.ts with no codegen between them.
This file is the third copy, and it is the one both sides are checked against:
server/src/protocol.rs has an exhaustive match and client/src/protocol.test.ts
has an exhaustive Record, so adding a variant on either side fails to compile
until it is added here, and adding it here fails until both sides follow.
The Rust side holds TWO lists: the exhaustive match, which is what stops the
crate compiling, and KNOWN_CLIENT_TAGS / KNOWN_SERVER_TAGS, which is what this
file is actually compared against. Updating only the match compiles and then
fails the suite saying this file names a tag the server does not have.
What it does NOT cover is field-level drift. A renamed or dropped field inside
a variant keeps the same tag and passes this check; the server rejects the frame
at runtime, which is now a console.error and so fails a browser driver. Closing
that gap properly means sample payloads or codegen, and neither is built.
